title: OPEC+ tipped to raise production again but new quotas loom
gist: OPEC+ is expected to lift September quotas by roughly 188,000 bpd at its Sunday online meeting — likely the last of the current series and completing the unwind of the second of three cut packages — but the increase is largely symbolic because members lack the capacity and the export routes to deliver it. Russia is pumping about 9.0 mbd against a 9.8 mbd target amid Ukrainian drone strikes, Gulf exports are throttled by Iran's near-paralysis of the Strait of Hormuz, and the group faces difficult quota talks next year after the UAE's May 1 exit.

themes.theme: September quota hike and the end of the unwind

insights.claim: OPEC+ is expected to raise oil production quotas for September by about 188,000 barrels per day, following several months of similar hikes, according to Rystad Energy analyst Jorge Leon.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A specific, small increment — 188 kbd is immaterial against a war-disrupted market, so the headline should not move crude much on its own.
insights.quote: The enlarged Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries will likely increase production by 188,000 barrels per day, following several months of similar hikes
insights.locator: Saudi Arabia, Russia and five other members of OPEC+

insights.claim: The September increase is likely to be the last in the current series of OPEC+ production adjustments and would complete the unwinding of the second of three production-cut packages the group introduced.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Marks the end of the automatic monthly supply-add narrative — after September, incremental OPEC+ barrels require a fresh political decision.
insights.quote: However, the September increase is likely to be the last in the current series of production adjustments, he said.
insights.locator: However, the September increase is likely to be the last

insights.claim: Between late 2022 and 2023 OPEC+ cut output in three separate rounds totalling nearly six million barrels per day over falling-price concerns, then reversed strategy from 2025 by gradually raising production.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Roughly 6 mbd of nominal cuts remains only partly unwound, defining the theoretical spare-barrel overhang still sitting above the market.

insights.claim: Many OPEC+ members cannot produce as much oil as their official targets allow because of a decline in production capacity, making quota increases progressively less meaningful, per UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Treat OPEC+ quota headlines as sentiment, not supply — actual capacity, not paper targets, sets the balance.

insights.claim: Russian oil production is hovering around nine million barrels per day against a target of 9.8 million bpd, with its oil infrastructure repeatedly targeted by Ukrainian drone attacks.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: An 800 kbd shortfall in Russia alone exceeds four months of OPEC+ quota increases — the group's largest non-Gulf producer is a net drag on supply.
insights.quote: production is hovering at around nine million barrels per day -- compared with a target of 9.8 million barrels per day
insights.locator: And in Russia, whose oil infrastructure has been repeatedly targeted

insights.claim: Gulf countries have struggled to increase oil exports because of the near-paralysis of the Strait of Hormuz orchestrated by Iran during the Middle East war, despite a brief upswing in shipping traffic after a US-Iran memorandum of understanding signed in June 2026.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Export logistics, not wellhead capacity, is the binding constraint on Gulf supply — quota policy cannot fix it and only a Hormuz reopening can.
insights.quote: The Gulf countries have struggled to increase exports due to the near-paralysis of the Strait of Hormuz orchestrated by Iran during the war in the Middle East
insights.locator: The Gulf countries have struggled to increase exports

insights.claim: OPEC+ is currently running a process to set maximum sustainable capacity levels for all member states, which will underpin new production quotas starting next year.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Baseline capacity reassessment is the mechanism through which future market share is allocated — the key OPEC+ event to track after September.
insights.quote: "the group is undergoing a process in setting maximum sustainable capacity levels for all member states"
insights.locator: Currently, "the group is undergoing a process

insights.claim: Analysts at DNB Carnegie say OPEC+ faces potentially difficult talks over new production quotas beginning next year, once the September increase is complete.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Sets up a 2027 quota negotiation as a discrete risk event for oil, with disagreement risk skewed toward a market-share scramble.
insights.quote: OPEC+ "faces potentially difficult talks over new production quotas" starting next year following the September increase

insights.claim: The UAE withdrew from OPEC+ on May 1, 2026, saying the move serves its national interests and long-term strategic objectives, after years of announcing projects and investments to expand its pumping capacity that made strict OPEC+ limits hard to justify.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Capacity expansion is the mechanism that pulls producers out of the cartel — watch other members with growth ambitions, notably Iraq, for the same trajectory.
insights.quote: Abu Dhabi said it "serves our national interests and long-term strategic objectives"
insights.locator: Explaining the move, Abu Dhabi said

insights.claim: Rystad's Jorge Leon says OPEC+ cohesion is not at risk at this moment, but warns the UAE's May withdrawal has highlighted a weakness in the group's cohesion.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Cohesion risk is dormant rather than absent — a second defection would flip the oil market from managed supply to volume competition.

insights.claim: Iraq has expressed a desire to significantly boost oil production even as it remains unclear when OPEC+ as a group will actually be able to raise volumes.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Iraq is the candidate to press hardest in the 2027 baseline talks, a source of internal friction and potential quota-busting supply.
